entry.title: CSS: vi and vb use the element's own writing mode, not the root's
entry.content:
Description

The vi and vb entries on the <length> reference page and in the viewport units table on the "Numeric data types" guide said these units follow the root element's inline/block axis. They actually follow the writing mode of the element the unit is used on. This PR drops "root" from both pages, and on the <length> page adds one sentence saying the axis comes from that element's writing-mode.

Motivation

On a page where one element has writing-mode: vertical-rl and the root is horizontal, the current wording tells readers vi on that element measures the viewport width. It measures the height. The linked issue has a live example.

Additional details

  • CSS Values 4 editor's draft defines the vi/svi/lvi/dvi and vb/... units as being "in the box's inline axis" / "block axis": https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#viewport-relative-lengths
  • The draft's changes section says: "Switched *vi and *vb units to resolve against the computed writing mode of the element itself. (Issue 6873)": w3c/csswg-drafts#6873 (comment)

Checked locally: prettier 3.10.1 and markdownlint-cli2 0.24.1 (the versions in package.json) pass on both files. I did not run a full local rari build. I used AI help to prepare this and checked the spec text myself.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46723

entry.title: Complete the "Data in WebGL" guide
entry.content:
Description

This PR fills the placeholder sections of the "Data in WebGL" page (varyings, uniforms, buffers, and textures) with explanations and code examples, and fixes the broken attributes example. In detail:

  • Attributes section
    • Fixed the code example, which used vec4() and flatten(). These functions don't exist in plain JavaScript, so the example now uses a Float32Array.
    • Renamed the attribute from vColor to aVertexColor and passed it on through the vColor varying (previously the undeclared fColor), to match the "Using shaders to apply color in WebGL" tutorial.
    • Rewrote the description text: attributes get one value per vertex, and only the vertex shader can declare and read them. Vertex positions were missing from the list of typical uses.
  • Varyings section
    • Added a code example.
    • Rewrote the description text: varyings are declared in both shaders, not only in the vertex shader, and their values are interpolated between the vertices.
  • Uniforms section
    • Added a code example.
    • Rewrote the description text: a uniform has the same value for a single draw call, not for the whole frame.
  • Buffers section
    • Added a code example.
    • Added the missing description text.
  • Textures section
    • Added a code example.
    • Added the missing description text.
  • Added a note that the code examples and terms on this page use GLSL ES 1.00 (WebGL 1), and how the syntax differs in GLSL ES 3.00.

Motivation

The page doesn't state that it's unfinished or a work in progress. It was imported from the old wiki as a draft in 2020, and the draft banner was removed in #10504, but the placeholders stayed. The code example didn't work, and explanations were missing. After the changes in this PR, readers can get a better understanding of the different data types in WebGL and how to use them with shaders. Readers who are interested in more in-depth details can follow the links to other MDN resources on the topic.

Personal motivation

I'm currently taking a university course on advanced web development. I used the MDN documentation for other assignments in that course, so I wanted to give something back to the community.

Additional details

Regarding the note

In the issue, I asked whether a note about the terms that changed in GLSL ES 3.00 is needed. So far, nobody has answered. In my opinion, the note is useful, but I'm happy to change or remove it.

Testing

  • I built a small test page that renders a triangle with a gradient between three vertex colors. It uses the examples from the attributes, varyings, uniforms, and buffers sections and works in Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.
  • A second test page renders a square with a 2×2 texture to check the textures example. It works in Edge.
  • The local preview shows no flaws, and Prettier, markdownlint, and cspell pass.

Sources

Checked against the GLSL ES 1.00 specification (sections 4.1.7 and 4.3.3–4.3.5), the WebGL 1.0 specification (bindBuffer(), vertexAttribPointer(), uniform*()), and, for the note, the GLSL ES 3.00 specification.

Use of AI

I used an AI assistant (Claude) to help translate parts of the text. I reviewed all changes, checked them against the specifications, and tested the examples.

Possible follow-up

The tutorial "Adding 2D content to a WebGL context" says that data can be stored in "varyings or attributes" to be shared with the fragment shader, but attributes are only available in the vertex shader. I could fix this in a separate PR.

Related issues and pull requests

  • Fixes #46631

entry.title: build(deps-dev): bump the npm-dev group across 1 directory with 3 updates
entry.content:
Bumps the npm-dev group with 3 updates in the / directory: cspell, markdownlint-cli2 and parse-diff.

Updates cspell from 10.5.1 to 10.5.2

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.5.2

Fixes

fix: --gitignore skips nested repositories in ignored folders again (#9648)

Summary

With --gitignore (useGitignore), cspell again skips a git repository kept in a folder that .gitignore excludes, such as a tool's cache of cloned dependencies. Since 10.4.0, these files were checked. A submodule in an ignored folder is still checked, as git does.

Fixes #9645

Before and after

A project with a clone in an ignored cache folder, and a submodule in an ignored vendor/ folder:

project/
  .gitignore     .cache/ and vendor/
  .gitmodules    lists vendor/lib
  README.md
  .cache/dep/    a clone, with its own .git
  vendor/lib/    a submodule

Before, cspell checked the clone:

$ cspell lint --gitignore --dot "**/*.md"
.cache/dep/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Thsi) fix: (This)
.cache/dep/NOTES.md:1:9 - Unknown word (misspeled) fix: (misspelled)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Anothr) fix: (Another)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:8 - Unknown word (typpo) fix: (typo)
CSpell: Files checked: 3, Issues found: 4 in 2 files.

After, it skips the clone and checks the submodule:

$ cspell lint --gitignore --dot "**/*.md"
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Anothr) fix: (Another)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:8 - Unknown word (typpo) fix: (typo)
CSpell: Files checked: 2, Issues found: 2 in 1 file.

What to know:

  • A repository in an ignored folder is skipped with all its files, unless .gitmodules lists it as a submodule.
  • A repository added with plain git add, without a .gitmodules entry, is skipped too.

entry.title: Clarify the response format for HTTP 423 Locked
entry.content:
Description

Explain what 423 Locked means for the requested operation and scope the XML response guidance to WebDAV.

Motivation

APIs such as Microsoft Graph use 423 Locked and document their own response format. Readers should be able to distinguish the status code from WebDAV's XML error format. Microsoft Graph error documentation

Additional details

RFC 4918 describes locked source or destination resources and recommends a precondition or postcondition code in a WebDAV response. RFC 4918, section 11.3

entry.title: CSSPerspective: fix pages and add examples
entry.content:
This updates CSSPerspective, its constructor, and its length property (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs).
  • Add a Description covering what a perspective does, the length values (a <length> or the keyword none), is2D (always false; setting it has no effect), and what toString() and toMatrix() return.
  • Fix length, which said that a value of 0 or a negative number applies no perspective. A length smaller than 1px is treated as 1px, and the keyword none applies no perspective.
  • Add the constructor's return value, and give its parameter type.
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that changes the perspective of a rotated box.

This covers the CSSPerspective items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec doesn't define any steps for setting length, but Chromium and Firefox convert the string "none" to a CSSKeywordValue and throw a TypeError for other values (as the WPT tests expect). The docs don't mention setter behavior.
  • BCD says Chrome supports CSSPerspective from version 66, but Chrome only accepts none from version 97. BCD has no subfeature for this.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594

entry.title: Sec-Fetch-Dest: explain values for navigations through a service worker
entry.content:
Description

This PR fixes the document directive on the Sec-Fetch-Dest page.
It no longer says "user-initiated".
It also adds a section about navigations that pass through a service worker.
The FetchEvent page gets a second example, "Opting out of iframe navigations".
The Sec-Fetch-User page gets a short section about the same case.
All three pages link to each other.

Motivation

A document request is not always user-initiated.
User activation is what Sec-Fetch-User reports.

Servers often use Sec-Fetch-Dest: document to detect top-level navigations.
This breaks when a service worker forwards the navigation with event.respondWith(fetch(event.request)).
The new section explains what the server sees in that case and how it tells top-level and iframe navigations apart.
Many service workers only serve and cache top-level navigations.
The FetchEvent example shows how such a service worker opts out of iframe navigations, so they keep Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe.

Additional details

  • A passthrough fetch sends Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty for top-level navigations and for iframe navigations.
  • Per the Request() constructor, that fetch keeps the mode navigate. The mode changes to same-origin only when init is not empty.
  • The pages describe the spec behavior only. Browser differences are left out.
  • A passthrough fetch does not send Sec-Fetch-User, even after a user click.
  • The WPT test service-workers/service-worker/navigation-headers.https.html expects navigate / empty for passthrough iframe navigations.

Related issues and pull requests

  • Spec discussion: w3c/ServiceWorker#1803
  • Firefox sends same-origin for the passthrough fetch today: Bugzilla 2035038
